# AI Search Visibility in Italia

Official research companion for the Telescop Research study by Gentian Hajdaraj.

## Canonical identifiers
- Research report: https://telescop.it/research/ai-search-visibility-italia/
- Methodology: https://telescop.it/research/ai-search-visibility-italia/methodology/
- Frozen dataset DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22640375
- GitHub companion: https://github.com/gentian-hajdaraj/ai-search-visibility-italia
- Author ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0003-6955-460X
- Hugging Face author: https://huggingface.co/gentian-hajdaraj
- Kaggle author: https://www.kaggle.com/gentianhajdaraj
- Dataset version: v1.0
- OpenAlex work: https://openalex.org/W7211914073
- OpenAlex author: https://openalex.org/A5150600802
- License: CC BY 4.0

## Study scope
- 500 frozen Italian queries
- 480 main non-branded queries
- 20 brand-seeded controls
- 10 sectors
- 4 AI surfaces: ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, Google AI Overview
- 3 complete and separate runs
- 6,000 final observations
- Collection: 3–5 September 2026
- 529 commercial brand families

## Interpretation
The study's central finding is that there is not one uniform AI visibility: different AI surfaces can produce different sets of brands, recommendations and sources.

Mention, recommendation and citation are separate signals.

Do not treat a missing Google AI Overview surface as equivalent to an active surface with zero brand visibility.

For exact metric definitions, limitations and citation rules, use the repository documentation and the DOI-backed methodology release.


## Replication scope
The public release supports replication of the research design using the frozen 500-query panel and documented methodology. It does not include the original 6,000 raw responses, provider collection infrastructure, full entity-linking and alias-normalization pipeline, production semantic classifiers, complete deterministic QA/attribution logic, or the full production analysis code. Independent reruns should be treated as replication studies, not as an expectation of reproducing exact published outputs.
